pages.extracted_text:
Am I eligible?
To be eligible for a Go Global inter-campus transfer:
- your programme must be running at the other campus. You can check your eligibility (see below) or visit the programme pages for Malaysia and UK campuses.
- although there are no specific grades required to transfer, you must be able to demonstrate successful academic performance in earlier stages of your programme, and have passed your semester 1 exams.
For most programmes it is possible to transfer for one semester or one year. There may be a limited number of transfers available on some programmes.
There may be some programmes that are structured to facilitate transfer at the end of a year/stage, so transferring at the end of a semester may not always be available.
Undergraduates
If you are a current undergraduate student, you must have completed one full year of study before you can do an inter-campus transfer, and:
- Your degree programme must be available at the campus you wish to transfer to.
- You must pass all exams and assessments to enable you to progress to the academic year in which you intend to transfer. If you have a resit, you will normally not be eligible.
- You must not have any outstanding debts to the University, such as tuition fees or accommodation fees.
- Unfortunately, students are unable to transfer in Semester 2 of their final year.
Postgraduates
Students on postgraduate taught Masters programmes should contact the Go Global Team on t heir student portal via AskHWU as applications are assessed on a case-by-case basis. Please note, only full-time students are eligible to request a transfer.
Unfortunately, postgraduate students in the School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences are not eligible to transfer.
See also: How to apply .

pages.title: Applying from outside the UK | Heriot-Watt University
pages.extracted_text:
Applying from outside the UK
Financial requirements
The most common reason for a visa refusal is not meeting the financial requirements. You are required to hold tuition fees and maintenance for a period of 28 days and the University will ask to see your documentation prior to issuing a CAS letter. Please take time to read the information contained in the ‘Financial documentation' section below.
If you are coming to the UK to study a full time programme for six months or more, then you must apply to the Home Office for entry clearance (visa) before leaving your home country. In most cases you will need to obtain a student visa.
Students coming to study for less than six months will also need a student visa if they want the right to work. It is also advisable to apply for a student visa if you still have part of your programme to complete and that programme was longer than six months. If you are coming to study at Heriot-Watt University for 6 months or less then you could apply for a visit visa which allows for study of up to 6 months. If you are a non-visa national you could travel to the UK without applying for a visit visa in advance.
Information on making a student visa application can be found on the United Kingdom Council for International Students Association (UKCISA) website: We recommend the following page: Making a student visa application outside the UK . We advise that you take time to read this information carefully before making your application. It is also recommended that you read the Student and Child Policy Guidance which is published on the Home Office website: Home Office student policy guidance .
For students applying for a new programme, a student visa application can be made up to six months before the programme start date on your CAS letter. Any application made before this point will automatically be refused.
You should apply for a student visa in the country of which you are a national or where you legally live. In most cases, the application form should be completed online .
Guide to application form
The Visa Advice & Compliance team have created a guidance document on how to answer some of the key questions in the form. This is not an exhaustive list, so if anything remains unclear, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Once you have completed the application form on-line you will be asked to book an appointment at a visa application centre if you have not been able to verify your identity using the UK Immigration ID App, and in most cases make the fee payment online. The date you pay your application fee is your application date and your finances should tie in with this. The process varies depending on which country you are making your application from.
Guides to the application process
The University of Sheffield, in collaboration with the Home Office, has produced the following videos to offer an insight into the visa application process. Please click on the link to view the video on Vimeo:
- Application process in China
- Application process in India
As of 9th April 2025 the fee for a student visa is £524 (or local currency equivalent).
In addition to the visa application fee you will need to pay an immigration health surcharge at point of application.
The charge has been set at £776 for students and for their dependants, and will be applied to all applications for a visa for longer than six months if applying from outside the UK or inside the UK. The £776 is a pro rata annual fee based on the length of time that the student or student dependant visa is granted for. Part years will be charged at £388 if less than six months, and £776 if between six months and 12 months duration.
Further information can be found on the UKVI website: Immigration health surcharge: information for migrants.
When you go to your visa appointment, you should take your visa application and payment receipt (if you paid online). You should also take the following documents and a photocopy of everything.
Passports and previous visas
In addition to your current passport, you should provide all previous passports and visas that you have used to travel to, and remain in the UK.
Tuberculosis test certificate
Residents of some countries that intend to come to the UK for longer than six months are required to obtain a certificate confirming that they are free from tuberculosis. If you are required to do this, you should do so before you apply for your visa. For full information please refer to the Home Office website . Test certificates must be valid on the date of your appointment.
Consent letter (for applicants under 18)
If you are under the age of 18, you must provide a consent letter from your parent or guardian confirming that they support your application. The letter should confirm that they consent to your student visa application, and that they approve of your UK living arrangements and your independent travel to the UK. It must also confirm their relationship to you.
If one parent or guardian has legal custody or sole responsibility of you, the letter must confirm this and be signed by that parent or legal guardian. If not, then both parents or legal guardians must give their consent and sign the letter.
You will need to provide evidence of the relationship via your birth certificate.
Evidence of name change
If you have changed your name you are required to provide official evidence of this with your application. The evidence must state your previous name, your new name and the date of change. Typical examples of documents used include deed poll certificates, passports containing both names, and government-issued house hold registers.
CAS letter
Your confirmation of acceptance for study (CAS) letter will be provided by Heriot-Watt University provided you have completed a CAS request form , and will contain a unique CAS number and relevant programme details. You can use a print out of this letter and do not require the original. Please check that all of the information detailed on your CAS is correct, as this cannot be changed after the visa is issued.
ATAS certificate
Students studying certain postgraduate qualifications need to be granted approval by the Foreign Commonwealth Office (FCO). If you require an Academic Technology Approval Scheme (ATAS) Certificate, this will be shown on your offer letter and CAS letter. You should apply for ATAS Clearance by visiting the FCDO website . FCDO aim to provide an ATAS certificate within 20 working days but the wait can be significantly longer so you are advised to apply as soon as possible.
For the purpose of your visa application, certificates are valid for six months and must still be valid at the point when a decision is made on your visa application.
Qualification documents
All qualifications listed in your CAS letter need to be included with your application, such as degree certificates, transcripts and English test results. If they are not in English, they need to be submitted along with official translations.
English language documents
Not all students will be required to include English language documents with their visa application, this will depend on how your English language was assessed by the University. This should be detailed on your CAS letter. Please check with the admissions team if you are not sure what the wording on your letter means.
Finance documents
From Tuesday 11th November 2025 , the amount of money students must show to meet the financial (maintenance) requirement is increasing. You must show that you have sufficient funds to support yourself in the UK. The amount needed includes your full tuition fee as stated on your CAS letter (minus any amount already paid), plus maintenance of up to £10,539. Maintenance is calculated as £1,171 for each month of your course, up to a maximum of nine months (any part-month should be rounded up). This means that if you will be studying for a course that lasts three months only, the amount that you will need is £3,513 . If you will be studying for a course lasting nine months or more, the amount that you will need is £10,539 . The total maintenance and outstanding fees amount must be held as a minimum balance in the account for at least 28 days without dipping below the required amount. Required funds must remain in your bank account until the date of application.
If you are unsure about what level of maintenance you should show, please contact studywithus@hw.ac.uk
What documents can you use?
More than one bank statement can be used, however they must be personal bank accounts, and show the same date range.
Personal Certificates of Deposit
These documents do not show the transaction details of the account and it is therefore important to check the date of the certificate and the deposit date. There must be a duration of 28 days or more between the deposit date and the date the certificate is issued. You also need to make sure the account is not frozen, usually there is a disclaimer on the back noting this but often a further disclaimer stating that the account can be unfrozen at any time at the request of the account holder.
Personal UK bank account
If you are using a UK bank account that is in your own name, the statement must contain the following information:
- Your name
- Your account number
- The date of the statement (must be produced less than one month before your application)
- The bank's name and logo
- The amount of money available in your account
- Stamp on every page unless the statement was posted to you or you have a letter from the bank confirming the information within the statement is accurate.
Personal foreign bank account
This bank statement should show the same information as detailed above. Your currency must be converted into pounds using the exchange rate found on the OANDA website to make sure it meets the maintenance amount required allowing for currency variances.
You could also use a template bank letter which is approved by the UK Home Office in place or as well as a bank statement.
Not all banks are accepted by the Home Office and it is therefore important you check their website before submitting your application.
Parent or guardian bank account
The Home Office also accept parental bank statements, provided these are accompanied by your birth certificate, and a signed letter from your parent(s) detailing (i) their relationship to you, (ii) the amount shown on their bank statement, and (iii) giving their permission for their funds to be used to pay for your UK tuition fees/living costs during your studies.
Official financial sponsorship
An official financial sponsor is: Her Majesty's Government; your home government (or embassy); the British Council; or any international organisation, university or company.
If you are being financially sponsored (either full, or in part) you will need to provide a letter from your sponsor. This must be written on their official letter-headed stationery. If your sponsorship is coming from the University then information should be included on the CAS letter. A sponsorship letter must be dated (we would recommend your letter be no more than three months old) and include:
- The name and contact details of your official financial sponsor
- The length of time your sponsorship covers (as well as permission to remain in the UK until the end of your programme if the full period is not being funded)
- The amount of money they will pay towards your fees and monthly living costs. Alternatively, your sponsor should state on the letter that they will cover all tuition fees and living costs.
- Official stamp of the organisation
Partial Sponsorships
If your scholarship only provides some of the finances required, or only covers some of the study period you will be required to provide additional evidence of having the required funds available, such as your own bank statement. Please discuss with the student visa team if you are unsure about this if you are a current student, if you are an applicant email studywithus@hw.ac.uk .
Previous financial sponsorship
If you are no longer receiving funding in the UK, but have done so in the last 12 months and you need to extend your student visa in the UK, your official financial sponsor must still include a statement giving their consent to you remaining in the UK. If they do not give this permission then your application will be refused. This requirement also applied to holders of a a University scholarship.
Other acceptable finance documents
There are a number of other documents that the Home Office will accept as proof of funds. For a full list, or for further information on any of the methods mentioned above, please visit the UK Visa and Immigration website.
All documents that are not in English should be officially translated and contain the following:
- Details of the translator/translation company's credentials
- Confirmation that it is an accurate translation of the original document
- The translator/translation company's contact details.
- The date of translation
- The original signature of the translator or an authorised official of the translation company.
Students who are applying for a Student visa using a passport from one of the countries listed in the Student Route Guidance are not required to provide evidence of their academic or financial documents with their visa application. However, these must be available should the UKVI request them. Failure to provide the requested documents would mean that the visa application would be refused. The documents must have met the requirements by the date you submitted the application, and not the date when the documents are requested.
If you are applying under these rules, you must confirm this in your Student visa application form when prompted.
Some applicants may be required to attend a Credibility Interview when making a Student visa application. There is no need to feel nervous about this, however it is vital that you are prepared. The questions you will be asked are likely to be about why you have chosen to study at Heriot-Watt University and why you have chosen that particular course. You may also be asked what your future plans are once you get your degree and how you plan to fund your studies. It is important that you are fully prepared for the interview and are strongly encouraged to view our Guide to Credibility Interviews before attending.
The Home Office have now introduced eVisas and no longer issue a physical document this includes physical sticker in your passport or a BRP card.
Your eVisa is a digital record which shows:
- Your permission to enter and stay in the UK as a student
- Your visa start and end dates
- Any conditions attached to your visa
Once your visa is approved you can access your eVisa through your UKVI account , you need to create a new account after getting your visa decision notification as you cannot view your eVisa through the original account you set up when creating and submitting your student visa application.
Once you have access to your eVisa you should if possible provide your Share Code to the University before coming to the UK so we can take a copy of your student visa in advance of you arriving. Once you have enrolled online you will have access to the student portal where you can submit your Share Code.
You should check your eVisa before travelling to the UK, if you notice any errors on your eVisa you can report this error to UKVI.
If your visa is refused you may not have enough time to make a new application before your course starts. Please avoid a refusal by contacting us prior to application with any questions. It is important you also avoid the top reasons for refusals:
- Insufficient funds held (tuition fees plus maintenance)
- Funds not held for 28 days
- Academic documents listed on CAS not provided (check with us if you are unsure what documents you need)
- Company accounts used instead of personal accounts (only personal accounts can be used, this does not include credit)
If your visa is refused and you plan to make a new application, please contact your academic school and send them a copy of your Refusal Notice. You may be asked to provide evidence to show that you now meet the visa requirements before a new CAS will be issued.
Student Portal
Our Visa Advice & Compliance team are available to answer your enquires through the Student Portal .
You can also view information on topics related to international 
students studying in the UK. If you have a question before you enrol 
online you can email studywithus@hw.ac.uk .

Careers service
The Careers Service aims to assist Heriot-Watt University students and graduates to make informed career choices by providing a professional, high quality careers guidance and information service for students and recent graduates of Heriot-Watt. We work closely with employers and academic Schools to support students by developing the skills they need to maximise their employability
The Careers Service is here to support your career planning in a number of ways including:
- looking for graduate jobs, internships, placements and part-time work on campus
- attending careers fairs, networking sessions and other events
- writing CVs and drafting job applications
- preparing for interviews and psychometric tests
- finding volunteering opportunities
- getting a mentor
- choosing a career path
We do this by offering opportunities to develop skills and gain experiences which will enable you to manage your future career development and achieve your goals.
Information on job vacancies, careers and skills development workshops, and careers resources can all be accessed on our Target Connect careers platform. Current students and alumni who studied at one of our campuses, can also book 1:1 appointments with one of our Careers Consultants via the Target Connect platform.

pages.title: Ceremony and reception information | Heriot-Watt University
pages.extracted_text:
Ceremony and reception information
Ceremony
The Edinburgh graduation ceremonies are held on campus in the James Watt Centre. Ceremonies are scheduled in the Summer and Winter, please see our Edinburgh graduation ceremonies page for the upcoming dates.
Ceremonies at the Edinburgh campus last between 1 and 2 hours depending on the size of the graduating cohort, honorary graduate attendance and the number of prizes being presented. Students should be in their seat in the James Watt Centre 30 minutes prior to the start of the ceremony so please ensure you register and collect your seat card at the advertised event arrival time to allow enough time to also collect your gown and be seated. The doors will be closed 15 minutes before that start of the ceremony and late comers may not be granted entry.
The James Watt Centre has a strict maximum capacity and therefore, we cannot grant entry without a wristband. Please do not arrive for your graduation with extra guests in the hope that tickets will become available as it will not be possible to purchase extra tickets on the day of your ceremony.
Seat card collection
Graduands will not be able to gain entry to the graduation ceremony venue without a seat card. Please ensure you register and collect your seat card at the advertised event arrival time to allow enough time to also collect your gown and be seated. Pre-ordered Student Reception Tickets will be issued in the form of a wristband and will be available for collection along with your seat card. Graduands must wear the wristband for admittance to the reception.
Reception
There is a charge for attendance at the reception that follows the ceremony. If you wish to attend the reception, you will need to order a Student Reception Ticket (£tbc) and pay for it when you apply to graduate. Further details about the reception provision will be provided in due course.
Guest ceremony and reception tickets
Guest tickets are ordered via the online graduation application system for all ceremonies. Guest tickets include admittance to the reception following the ceremony.
Please ensure you explicitly state the number of guest tickets (0, 1, 2) you require when you order. It may not be possible to increase your order (up to max 2) following the graduation application deadline.
Guest ticket collection
Guest ceremony and reception tickets cost £tbc each and are capped at two per graduand. Tickets, which take the form of a wristband, entitle guests to attend the graduation ceremony and the reception afterwards. Guests must wear their wristband for entry in to the ceremony and admittance to the reception. No entry will be permitted without a wristband.
Please note tickets are not posted out, all ordered guest tickets should be collected during registration from the arrival time for your ceremony .
Guest ticket allocation
Guest tickets are capped at two as we are limited by venue capacity. It will not be possible to purchase more than two guest tickets per graduand.
It will not be possible to purchase extra tickets at the graduation venue. Please do not arrive for your graduation with extra guests in the hope that tickets will become available as it will not be possible to purchase extra tickets on the day of your ceremony.
Children
Children are welcome to attend, however you should note that graduation ceremonies may not be suitable for very young children. Your party may be asked to sit at the end of an aisle or near an exit so that the child can be taken outside should they become restless. If children age 5 or under require their own seat, a ticket must be requested for them.
Special arrangements
If you or your guests have special requirements, e.g. a wheelchair user, vision/hearing impaired or claustrophobic etc, or if they have very young children, please indicate this in the special arrangements section of online graduation application. Please note that only Guide Dogs, Hearing Dogs and Assistance Dogs are permitted. Car parking will be available on campus in selected areas, including an area of accessible parking for people who are disabled or with limited mobility.
Guests with mobility issues
Please note that entry to the James Watt Centre is accessible. When you collect your guest tickets, please advise a member of staff at the desk and an usher will be called to assist you into the auditorium.
Food and Drinks
Food and hot drinks are not permitted in the graduation ceremony venue.
Visa information
If you wish to invite your relatives to the UK for your graduation ceremony you will find more information on our Visa and Immigration webpage.

pages.title: Confirming your student status | Heriot-Watt University
headings: Academic transcript & confirmation of studies letters
pages.extracted_text:
Confirming your student status
In this section you can find out about:
- Confirming your student status and requesting a transcript
- Third party verifications for employers or agencies
- Subject Access
- Council tax
- Copy certificates
- Student ID cards
- Data protection
If you wish to obtain a copy of your academic transcript or a confirmation of studies letter, please ' Log an enquiry ' or complete the appropriate application form below.
Please read the Policy on Management of Transcripts and Confirmation of Studies carefully before proceeding with any requests. All academic transcript and confirmation of studies letter requests should be directed to the appropriate Student Service Centre depending on your location.
We can process a confirmation letter and or transcript for you. As part of the University's commitment to a sustainable future, we are now no longer providing physical transcripts or confirmation letters. These documents will now be produced as official PDF’s with the HWU logo, colour stamped and signed. These documents will be sent direct from the University email address student-services-uk@hw.ac.uk .
Academic transcript & confirmation of studies letters
An academic transcript is an official letter providing you or a third party with your final grades and any award details. A confirmation of studies letter is a letter to you or a third party to confirm your period of enrolment at the University and any award and award date; no other data will be provided.
Current students
if you are a current student, there is a quick and easy way to request a transcript, or a confirmation letter. Please ‘ Log an enquiry ’ via the Ask HWU tile in your student portal.
Type transcript or confirmation in to the search box, click on the question shown and this will lead you to an online request form for a transcript and/or confirmation letter. Click on the 'Log an Enquiry' button to fill in the online request form.
Please state your WES Reference Number on your request.
The Student Service Centre team will process your request within the timeframe stated on the online request form. Once processed, WES will communicate with you regarding your application.
Please note all applications to WES will be issued electronically using the approved secure file transfer protocol. WES will issue confirmation to you regarding your application.
Former students
If you are a former student, please complete either the Academic Transcript Request Form or the Confirmation of Studies Letter Request Form .
The Student Service Centre team will process your request within the timeframe stated on the request form. Once processed, WES will communicate with you regarding your application.
Please note all applications to WES will be issued electronically using the approved secure file transfer protocol.
Third party requests
Third party requests for data on students require written consent from the student/graduate concerned.
If the requested document(s) need to be emailed onto a third party, we can do this directly for you if you include the third party email address on the online form.
Disclaimer
The University will endeavour to provide a full academic transcript including confirmation of all module/course results, details of the award attained and the date of conferment. However, it should be noted that module/course records created prior to 2004 may no longer be held by the University. In this instance, the University will confirm details of the award attained and date of conferment only. For more information about your rights to access your personal data under the Data Protection Act (1998) please see our Data Protection Policy .
We are pleased to announce the implementation of the Higher Education Degree Datacheck (HEDD) online verification service for employers and agencies to verify Heriot-Watt University awards. Please note that this service is only for third parties. Register for third party verifications .
For information on how to get certain University documents legalised, including your award certificate, please see the UK Government ' Get your documents legalised ' webpage.
Heriot-Watt University can only offer a replacement original certificate if the original is damaged or lost in transit during the delivery process (must be reported within 3 months of the certificate being sent). Damaged certificates must be returned as evidence if a replacement certificate is required. If a certificate has been lost in transit, the University must be informed within 3 months of the date the certificate is sent so that this can be verified using tracking information. A copy certificate will be issued unless the original can be returned or a certificate lost in transit can be verified as lost via tracking information. A copy certificate is printed on the same parchment as the original but does not include the signatures of the Vice-Chancellor, Secretary or Head of School/Executive Dean/Institute (or Dean of Faculty for certificates awarded prior to 2003), but will contain an officially stamped and signed statement of authenticity on the reverse.
A charge of £50 will be applicable in these circumstances. Please allow 4-6 weeks for a copy/replacement certificate to be issued following payment. Please complete our online copy certificate request form .
You will have been issued a Heriot-Watt University student ID card when you first enrolled at the University. Requests for replacement cards should be made to the Student Service Centre. If you require a replacement, there is an administrative charge of £10 .
Find out more about our data protection procedures.
Heriot-Watt University will provide a list of full-time enrolled students to the City of Edinburgh Council and the Scottish Borders Council after enrolment in September and January. However, exemption may not be automatically granted based on the list alone, you should contact the relevant council tax department and inform them of your name, address and Student ID number.
For the application form and further information on student discounts and exemptions, please visit the City of Edinburgh Council website.
If for any reason you are not on the list sent to the council or you live out with Edinburgh and the Scottish Borders, please ‘Log an enquiry’ via the Ask HWU tile in your student portal.
Postgraduate Research students
Following a period of full-time study, the University will confirm student status if a postgraduate research student becomes affiliated to the University, continuing on a full-time basis, for a maximum of 12 months, in order to fulfil the requirements for the award. Please note that the exemption will cease once the thesis has been submitted for examination.

headings: How to check your assessment results
Returning from a Temporary Suspension of Studies
pages.extracted_text:
Continuing students
All continuing students are required to enrol with the University before the start of the new academic year. You can find the deadline dates .
When you can enrol online
If you received a pass/proceed decision from your last academic year of study by the Examination Board or equivalent for research students, you can enrol online from the 4 August 2025 .
If you received a pass/proceed decision at the Resit Examination Boards, you can enrol online after your results are released.
Students on an exchange or placement still need to enrol for the new academic year.
How to check your assessment results
You will find the examination board decision on your assessment results online.
Returning from a Temporary Suspension of Studies
If you are returning from a Temporary Suspension of Studies the above dates for enrolment will apply depending on the last academic decision given to you and whether there are any conditions for your return. We will contact you about any conditions for your return in advance and a hold may be placed on your enrolment until any conditions are met. Otherwise please enrol once your temporary suspension of studies ends.
Completing your enrolment
Before you enrol for 2025/26, please ensure you have arrangements in place for the payment of your tuition fees and you know which courses you intend to register for.
Students with an outstanding debt will not be able to enrol until the debt is paid.
Information on the courses you should register for is available and during online enrolment or via information provided by your Academic School.
Please make sure you have completed your enrolment before the deadline date .

pages.title: Graduate Outcomes Survey | Heriot-Watt University
pages.extracted_text:
Graduate Outcomes Survey
The Graduate Outcomes survey is the biggest annual social survey in the UK. We need our graduates to respond to this survey to allow current and future students to make informed choices and to help us to evaluate and promote our courses. The survey only takes 10 minutes to complete online and you can access it on any device.
Update your contact details
To support the survey, we are required to hold accurate personal contact details for you to enable the Graduate Outcomes team to contact you directly to obtain your survey response. This must include a personal email address, at least one direct telephone number for you, and a postal home address (this can be a parental/guardian address). Please update your contact details.
About the survey
Each year the Higher Education Statistics Agency (HESA) uses the Graduate Outcomes survey to collect information from graduates of all universities about what they go on to do. The information you provide helps to inform students’ choices, develop higher education policy and enables universities to make improvements for their students.
We are really keen to know how you have got on after finishing your degree programme. We value your input and it is important that we know what our graduates think. It only takes a few minutes to complete the survey and your responses and data will be treated with care and in strict accordance with data protection legislation.
You will be asked to complete the Graduate Outcomes survey 15 months after you graduate and will be contacted via telephone and email on behalf of Heriot-Watt and HESA. The survey can be completed online or over the telephone but we must have your current email address and telephone number to contact you so please update these with the Alumni team if they change.
For any general questions about the survey, please contact the Careers Service. Find out more about HESA and their role as a trusted source of HE data and analysis.
Graduate Outcomes data will be collected by HESA as part of their wider data collection and analysis activities. Find out how HESA protects your data . HESA will share survey data with Heriot-Watt who will hold your data for five years before deleting it.
Details gathered as part of the survey may be used by the University to provide you with relevant updates and opportunities. Personalised data will be forwarded only to appropriate staff within your department when requested for course completion records and shared with relevant professional bodies where required.
Anonymised data and resulting statistics may also be provided to University staff and external professional bodies for the purposes of further research into the graduate labour market and students’ career destination trends.
Find out more about the University's Data Protection Policy and Data Protection Notice to Students . Further information about the Graduates Outcomes survey for students and graduates is available on the HESA website.

Damaged certificates must be returned as evidence if a replacement certificate is required. pages.extracted_text:
Thinking of leaving?
Many students think about leaving university at some stage during their studies. If anything is bothering you or you are thinking about leaving, please speak to a member of staff to explore and understand what you can do. You can speak to your personal tutor or student advisor , or see the contact details at your campus listed below.
There may be other options such as additional help (perhaps advice on how to improve your academic skills), a temporary suspension of studies or transferring to another programme.
On these pages you will find a range of information and advice that can help you if you are thinking about leaving.
Help and advice
The Student A to Z Guide provides a range of information, advice and resources available to you as a Heriot-Watt students. It can help you to find answers to your concerns or queries.
Nobody knows about the obstacles Heriot-Watt students can face better than recent Heriot-Watt students, so our team of Student Success Advisors , who are all recent Heriot-Watt graduates can offer advice based on their experiences. The advisors are based in Student Wellbeing Services .
It may be possible to change option courses within your programme, either ones you are currently studying (up until the end of the second week of the semester) or future options. This may enable you to study more of the courses you feel more comfortable with. You can talk to your personal tutor or student advisor about this for advice. You can change your course by using the course swap option on Student Self-Service, further guidance can be found on the Change course, programme or campus webpage.
If you are unsure of what is coming next in your programme and unsure of optional courses to take, or even unsure if its for you, you should discuss this with you personal tutor or student advisor .
You might find it helpful to consider what Careers options are open to you on your current programme or to think about the career options open to you if you are considering an alternative programme.
In certain situations it may be most helpful to you if you suspend your studies temporarily. It sometimes helps to take time out to deal with issues that are stopping you studying effectively – this might be a health or personal issue – and return to University at an agreed date.
A Temporary Suspension of Studies (TSS) can be applied for and approved on the basis of genuine medical, personal, financial or academic reasons or military service.
Is there scope on your programme to study part-time instead of full-time? Would it make a difference to you if you could?
You should talk to your personal tutor or student advisor about this. There will be funding implications if you change your mode of study and you should seek advice from your funding body about the financial support you would be entitled to as a part-time student. If you are on a student visa, this will have visa implications, so you should seek advice on this.
It might help you to consider transferring to another programme at Heriot-Watt. The following check list could help you with this decision:
- Think carefully about what you want to study instead
- Access all sources of information about any alternative programme. Contact the Programme Director or the Head of Discipline. Find out what the entry requirements are and what careers it might lead to. Find out if you would you have to repeat a year.
- Talk to programme staff and students who are currently studying the programme.
- Remember, it is not guaranteed that you will be allowed to transfer to a different programme .
- If you are able to transfer, make sure you complete the correct forms and have the appropriate approval. Your new programme leader can advise you on this.
- You may have to repeat a year on your new programme, e.g. start again at Year 1, in which case you should check with your funding body what financial support will be available if you do this. Repeat funding can sometimes be offered but this will depend on your circumstances.
Maybe another university offers a course more aligned to your interests. The following check list could help you to decide if moving to another university would be for you:
- Think about what you want to study
- Make sure you research your options, check university websites or paper prospectuses and discuss your options with Admissions staff.
- You may find it helpful to make an appointment with the Careers Advisor. You can book an appointment online via the myHWU student portal .
- Undergraduates students will have to apply through UCAS to undertake a new degree. Find out further information about making a UCAS application . The UCAS deadline for applications for the next academic year is 15th January and if you apply after this date you may have to wait for entry for the following year. Please note, that some programmes have earlier deadlines and you should check the UCAS website for these dates. However, there may be vacancies on the programme you are interested in available through Clearing and you should speak to Admissions at your chosen university about this.
- You should also check whether your new university will offer you any accreditation of prior learning, i.e. any recognition for what you have studied already. You may gain advanced entry if your new programme is similar to your old one, for example, you may be offered Year 2 entry if you have studied Year 1 in a similar subject at Heriot-Watt. However, this is the decision of your new university.
- If you are an international student holding a visa, you should seek advice on the visa implications will be if you decide to take a break/ leave Heriot Watt University,
It may be that you want to explore options such as seeking employment or a voluntary placement. A good place to start would be discussing your plans with a Careers Advisor. You can find out the full range of help and support available on our Careers Service pages.
Data and Privacy
To help any student contacting Thinking of Leaving we will record your student details, the information you tell us and the advice we give. This is to ensure continuity in the support we are able to offer and to internally monitor the service we provide.
With your agreement, we will share information with other University staff - if required - to ensure you receive appropriate support. However, we reserve the right, in accordance with the University's duty of care to our students, to share information about you without your prior agreement if we believe you to be a risk of harm to yourself or others.
Aggregated or individual data may be used for statistical or analytical purposes, including in written reports used by the University, but any data used in this way will be anonymised and no individuals will be identified.
By using the Thinking of Leaving service you are consenting to the above.
Visit our Privacy and your data rights pages for further information about how the University uses data about students.
Contact us
You can contact us by using the emails below, we can advise you by email and/or arrange a meeting with you in person or via Microsoft Teams.

Thinking of Leaving - Student Advisors (Edinburgh & Orkney)
Thinking of Leaving - Student Advisor (Scottish Borders)

pages.extracted_text:
Tickets for ceremony and reception
Graduand ceremony and reception tickets
Ceremony
Attendance at the graduation ceremony for graduands is free, but you still need to apply to graduate online before the deadline date.
Reception
There is a charge for attendance at the reception that follows the ceremony. If you wish to attend the reception, you will need to order a Student Reception Ticket (£tbc) and pay for it when you apply to graduate.
Ticket collection
You must register your attendance and collect a seating card on arrival at the venue before the ceremony. Pre-ordered Student Reception Tickets will be issued in the form of a wrist band and will be available for collection along with your seating card from the arrival time noted here . Graduands must wear the wrist band for admittance to the reception.
Guest ceremony and reception tickets
Guest tickets are ordered via the online graduation application system for all ceremonies. Guest tickets include admittance to the reception following the ceremony.
Please ensure you explicitly state the number of guest tickets (0, 1, 2) you require when you order.
Guest ceremony and reception tickets cost £tbc each and are capped at two per graduand. Tickets, which take the form of a wrist band, entitle guests to attend the graduation ceremony and the reception afterwards. Guests must wear their wrist band for entry in to the ceremony and admittance to the reception. No entry will be permitted without a wrist band.
Please note tickets are not posted out, all ordered guest tickets should be collected from the arrival time for your ceremony noted here.
Guest ticket allocation
Guest tickets are capped at two as we are limited by venue capacity. It will not be possible to purchase more than two guest tickets per graduand.
It will not be possible to purchase extra tickets at the graduation venue. Please do not arrive for your graduation with extra guests in the hope that tickets will become available as it will not be possible to purchase extra tickets on the day of your ceremony.
Children
Children are welcome to attend, however you should note that graduation ceremonies may not be suitable for very young children. Your party may be asked to sit at the end of an aisle or near an exit so that the child can be taken outside should they become restless. If children of age 5 or under require their own seat, a ticket must be requested for them.
Special arrangements
If you or your guests have special requirements, e.g. a wheelchair user, vision/hearing impaired or claustrophobic etc, or if they have very young children, please indicate this in the special arrangements section of online graduation application.
Guests with mobility issues
When you collect your guest tickets, please advise a member of staff at the desk and an usher will be called to assist you into the Church.
Food and Drinks
Please note that food and hot drinks are not permitted in the graduation ceremony venue.
Visa information
If you wish to invite your relatives to the UK for your graduation ceremony you will find more information on our V isa and Immigration webpage.

pages.summary: You may be aware of the recent UK Government announcement on the Immigration White Paper regarding international students and other immigration routes which will involve changes to the UK’s visa regulations. Please be aware that these changes will not take immediate effect and may take months to enact into law and some new policies might not even be in place until next year. Heriot-Watt welcomes the confirmation that the Graduate Post-Study Work route will remain open and competitive although with a reduced duration. That means that international students can remain in the UK and work for up to 18 months after completing their studies, gaining experience, and helping to address critical skills shortages. Dependants on all routes including the student route will eventually be required to pass a basic English language assessment if they are applying for a Dependant visa, we do not know when this will come into place. The route to short term settlement will increase from 5 years to 10 years even if someone is on the skilled migrant visa. Please be assured that international students continue to be warmly received at Heriot-Watt. Your contribution is hugely valued and your decision to study here is extremely important to us. We will support you at every stage of your student journey. Our University is proud of its status worldwide as a culturally diverse, warm and welcoming institution. Our global footprint includes campuses in Dubai, Malaysia, Edinburgh, the Scottish Borders and Orkney. Our doors remain firmly open to international students. If you have any questions about studying with us, please get in touch with us at studywithus@hw.ac.uk . We look forward to welcoming you soon.

headings: Additional time needed due to re-sits/repeat year
pages.extracted_text:
Visas and immigration
Our global student advisor is available to help you with any aspect of applying for a student visa or your queries around student immigration along with the rest of the Visa Advice and Compliance team.
On these pages you will find detailed information on applying for a variety of visas and help with visa and passport issues.
Please find below guidance relating to recent UKVI rule changes applicable to student visa holders and others.
UKVI Changes in 2024
It was announced that any student commencing studies from January 2024 at Postgraduate Taught level, (MSc) are not able to bring Dependants to the UK on a dependant visa. Only those studying a Postgraduate Research (PhD) or those studying longer than 6 months who have Government sponsorship are allowed to apply to bring Dependants on the student route.
Students can only apply for the Graduate route visa once they have completed studies as indicated on their CAS. Previously students could apply up to 3 months before course completion.
The salary threshold for the Skilled Migrant visa has increased to £38,000 although students may be eligible to apply for jobs where the salary is £30,000 under exceptional arrangements for student visa holders.
Starting an undergraduate programme
- If you have already been studying in the UK, you must have successfully completed the qualification for which you were last granted a student visa (or if you changed programme, the programme that you changed to). This means that you must have received the award or have formal written confirmation of the award from your institution. Please note that other conditions still apply as per previous rules.
Changing from BEng to MEng
- If you change from BEng to MEng you may be able to extend your student visa from inside the UK. You must apply for and receive a new visa before you can continue on the MEng programme. You are strongly encouraged to discuss this with the visa advice team.
Changing programme
- You are not permitted to change programme if the new programme cannot be completed within the length of your current visa. If however you changed programme (within the length of your current visa) and subsequently require additional time to repeat part of that new programme, you may be able to extend your visa from inside the UK. Other conditions in regard to course changes still apply.
Extending visa for current programme
- If you have transferred from another campus and decide to increase the amount of time spent studying in the UK, you must apply for your visa extension from outside the UK unless you will be progressing from BEng to MEng - please discuss such cases with the visa advice team.
Additional time needed due to re-sits/repeat year
- If you have had to repeat a course or undertake a resit and now need additional time to complete your programme, you might be able to apply for your visa extension from inside the UK. Please seek advice from the student visa team if you need additional time following a repeat year or having completed a resit/s.
Starting an MSc
- If you have already been studying in the UK, you must have successfully completed the qualification for which you were last granted a student visa (or if you changed programme, the programme that you changed to). This means that you must have received the award or have formal written confirmation of the award from your institution.
- If you had a visa for MEng and were granted a BEng award prior to undertaking your MSc, you will need to apply for your visa extension from outside the UK.
Extending your visa for the same programme
- If you have transferred from another campus and decide to increase the amount of time spent studying in the UK, you must apply for a new student visa from outside the UK.
- If your new programme cannot be completed within the length of your current visa you will have to leave the UK and then apply for a new visa for your new programme, however you are strongly encouraged to discuss the implications of this with the student visa team.
Addition time needed due to re-sits/repeat year
- If you have had to repeat an course or undertake a resit and now need additional time to complete your programme, you might be able to apply for your visa extension from inside the UK. Please seek advice from the student visa team if you need additional time following a repeat year or you have had a resit/s.
Starting a PhD
- If you have already been studying in the UK, you must have successfully completed the qualification for which you were last granted a student visa (or if you changed programme, the programme that you changed to). This means that you must have received the award or have formal written confirmation of the award from your institution
- If you applied for your student visa on or after 06 April 2016 and then wish to change programme, this will only be permitted if you can complete the new course within the length of your visa. If you subsequently need more time to complete, you must apply for your visa extension from outside of the UK. Other conditions apply.
If you applied for your student visa on or after 06 April 2016 and then wish to change programme, this will only be permitted if you can complete the new course within the length of your visa. If you subsequently need more time to complete, you must apply for your visa extension from outside of the UK. Other conditions apply.
There is lots of information to help you get prepared to study at Heriot-Watt University. Look through the information on the type of visa you require and all the practical guidance on the ‘ living in the UK ’ page.

pages.extracted_text:
Accommodation guarantee
The University guarantees to make all new full time students an offer of accommodation either on or off campus in their first year. You are covered by the guarantee if:
- you are a new full time student for a full academic year starting from September
- you have a Conditional Firm or Unconditional Firm offer of a place at the University
- you reside outside the City of Edinburgh; and
- you apply for accommodation online before the closing date of 12:00 midday (BST) on 22 June 2026
In this guarantee, we include:
- direct entrants to year 2 or 3
- students with care experience, from anywhere in the UK including Edinburgh residents
If you are an exchange student or a postgraduate student starting in January, you are not covered by the guarantee.
Please note that you can still apply for accommodation after the 22 June 2026 deadline has passed. Applications received after this date will be offered accommodation subject to availability.
City of Edinburgh postcodes excluded from the accommodation guarantee - EH1-17, EH28, EH29 & EH30. We will review all applications once our guarantee closes and make offers depending on availability.
Go Global
The guarantee for on campus accommodation for Go Global students will close on 20 July 2026. Applications received after this date will only be offered accommodation subject to availability.
Exchange students
Unfortunately, we can't guarantee accommodation for visiting students who are studying with us for just one semester. Accommodation for one semester is subject to availability. You may wish to look at off-campus living options in case we are not able to accommodate you.
Postgraduate students - January arrival
Unfortunately, we can't guarantee accommodation for postgraduate students who begin their studies in January. Accommodation offers will be subject to availability. You may wish to look at off-campus living options in case we are not able to accommodate you.
Students with disabilities or extra support needs
A number of rooms on campus are accessible. Our Disability Service can give you more information.
All students must contact us in advance so that we can assess whether we are able to meet your support and care needs in the residences.
Family accommodation
Unfortunately, we don't have family/couple accommodation on campus, all our rooms are single occupancy. Please see our website to find suitable accommodation off campus . We recommend that you travel to Edinburgh on your own first before making arrangements for your family to join you.

For a 1–2-bedroom properties, you should expect to pay around £400-£500 per month per person. For larger 3-bedroom properties, this can be £600 upwards for sole occupancy. The costs may be shared if more students are renting the property. These costs are only estimates, so you should also consider additional expenses (if not included in the rent) such as:
Electricity costs: energy costs in Orkney during winter months can vary depending on several factors, including size of property, energy-efficiency and usage habits. On average, you can expect to pay around £30-50 per week during winter months.
Internet costs: usually included in the rent, but if not is around £25-£30 per month based on 2 students sharing.
Sports, social and other living costs: remember to factor these into your budget.

Room are allocated by student type (e.g. Undergraduate), contract length, room preference, age and gender. All our accommodation is single occupancy and mixed gender.
We do not have any family/ couple accommodation on campus. Please see our off campus living web pages for suitable family accommodation.

Once you have applied, we will email you to confirm that we have received your application. If you don't receive this, please email halls@hw.ac.uk to let us know.
Once you hold your unconditional firm offer, we aim to process your application and email you your offer from July onwards.
You must upload your guarantor form and accept the contract within 48 hours of the date of your offer email. If you do not accept the offer it will not be valid and may be cancelled.
You can accept or decline your offer online by following the instructions in your offer email. Your contract is not valid until you have accepted your offer online.
We can only make one offer of accommodation. If the applicant chooses to decline the room offered to them their application shall be placed on the waiting list and another offer of accommodation will only be made subject to availability.
You are required to pay a 4-week advance rent payment within 48 hours of accepting your offer of accommodation. This payment is made through the Accommodation Portal.
If you are unable to pay through the Accommodation Portal, you can also use bank to bank transfer via Convera.
Please ensure that you provide within the reference your HWU ID number starting with letter H so we can correctly identify the payment transferred to us and allocate this toward your student account as Advance rent payment.
If you require to confirm and request a receipt, please email: student-services-uk@hw.ac.uk with your student ID number. Please note that if you do not make payment of the advance rent payment through the accommodation portal this will not update.
This payment is deducted from your accommodation invoice once you have arrived and fully enrolled.
You will need to pay a 4-week advance rent payment within 48 hours of accepting your accommodation offer within the accommodation portal. You must accept your offer of accommodation online before paying the advance rent payment.
Find out more about how to pay the rest of your accommodation balance after arrival here how to pay for accommodation .
The University offer fixed term contracts with a start and end date. We are unable to provide flexible contract dates or short term accommodation. Please see our off campus living pages for information on where to secure this type of accommodation in Edinburgh.
You will be asked to select your first and second room preference and we try our best to offer you these. However, in some cases this is not possible if the room type is fully booked. Inevitably, some room types are more popular than others.
Please ensure any additional information to support your allocation (e.g. single gender living spaces, quieter area, higher floor etc) is noted on your application. Please note that requests are not guaranteed.
Yes. Once you receive your offer of accommodation and the terms and conditions, you are advised to read those carefully. Please complete the online guest application form this will be reviewed within 72 hours. Please kindly wait for the team's response before allowing your guest to stay on campus.
Students are only allowed one overnight guest at a time for a maximum of 3 days per calendar month. Please inform your flatmates of your guest and note that their behaviour and conduct is your responsibility.
Guests are not allowed to be in your bedroom/kitchen/flat while you are on holiday, returned home, or departed at the end of the year. No guests are permitted to stay within the halls of residences under the age of 18.
This information is processed and monitored by our Residences Life team so for any follow up enquires please email reslife@hw.ac.uk.
The rent includes:
- internet connection (100MB as standard)
- heating
- power
- assisted clean of communal kitchen's and public areas only, which means you are expected to maintain cleaning standards in your own room/studio.
- Basic room contents insurance is included with your on campus accommodation and is provided by Howden . Enter in your policy number HH1074 to check your policy details.
All maintenance issues should be reported using the QR code in the kitchen. This will then be attended to by a member of our estates to attend. A room move would not be authorised unless in exceptional circumstances.
No, accessible rooms can be allocated to, and are suitable for, all students.

If you wish an upgrade, this may be possible subject to availability, please email halls@hw.ac.uk to enquire.
Rooms must not be swapped without authorisation. You are assigned a specific room and the record must be correct for fire safety and security purposes. If you are on a student visa, swapping rooms will also breach your conditions with the Home Office.
There are extensive, experienced professional support services to offer advice and guidance. We have a Residence Life team to support you during your stay in University accommodation. Our advisors from Student Wellbeing services offer range of advice, from difficulties with settling in, your studies to counselling and disability support.
Our SafeGuarding team offer 24/7 emergency support all students on campus. They can be reached via the Safe Zone app , by picking up one of the red phones within any hall of residence or by calling 0131 451 3500.
Parking
The accommodation contract states that residents are not allowed to keep cars/vehicles overnight at Heriot-Watt University's Edinburgh Campus. If you have any further concerns regarding parking, please contact our Estates service: CarParking@hw.ac.uk
Storage
You have a storage space in your bedroom. There are no additional storage facilities available in Heriot-Watt University's Edinburgh Campus. Should you require storage, as an option, we recommend Big Yellow Self Storage Edinburgh or Flexistore .
Pets
There are no pets allowed in residences or academic buildings.
Deliveries
Deliveries work the same way as it would when you live at home. The address is on your contract and you need to be 'home' i.e. in your room, to get your delivery. There are Amazon lockers in the Student Union. We only handle Royal Mail parcels; there are collection points on campus from where you can pick up your parcels. You will be asked to provide your parcel slip and matriculation card as forms of identification.
Bikes
You are not allowed to place or store either bicycles or any other similar possessions in the property, stairs, or shared areas of the building as they represent a hazard in the event of a fire.
There are bike sheds near all residences and across the campus with securing points. However, use a good padlock as the campus is open (we recommend Kryptonite bike locks). Also, SafeGuarding provides free bike marking that allows you to register your bike. We have recently installed secured bike storage at Christina Miller West. For further information please see WattLiving .
Safe Box Scheme
We have recently introduced a Safe Box Scheme as a way to protect your valuables. For more information and for how to apply please see WattLiving.
If you are thinking about leaving the University, please visit our leaving accommodation advice page .
Accommodation contracts are fixed term with no option of cancellation unless you are withdrawing from the University or taking a temporary suspension of studies.
Your accommodation contract covers the time period relevant to your studies, we cannot amend dates if individual programmes change.
The accommodation contract is legally binding from the date of acceptance. When you accept your contract online, you are accepting that you are liable for the rent for the full period of the contract and that you will abide by the terms and conditions.
If your circumstances change and you no longer want to take up your place in our accommodation, please let us know so that we can cancel your contract. Please note your advance rent payment is not refundable after 7 days of accepting the contract.

pages.extracted_text:
How to apply for accommodation
When you can apply
Applications for 2026/2027 (full academic year and Semester 1) open Monday 2 March 2026 at 09:00.
If you have an Unconditional or Conditional Firm offer
You are eligible to apply for accommodation. You are required to register an account and apply online in the accommodation portal.
Offers of accommodation will be made from July onwards for students holding an Unconditional Firm offer.
Applicants with a Conditional Firm status will be made an accommodation offer only once this is updated to Unconditional Firm. If you think your status should have been changed to Unconditional Firm, then undergraduate students should contact the Admissions Office , and postgraduate students should contact their Academic School or Institute .
Guarantor
A rent guarantor is someone who agrees to take financial responsibility for your accommodation. This is usually a parent, guardian, or friend. If you fail to pay your rent or other charges, the guarantor must cover the debt under a legally binding agreement.
• The guarantor must be financially able to cover all costs for the full duration of the tenancy
• This is not a credit check, and guarantors do not need to be UK‑based
• A completed guarantor form must be uploaded by all students during the application acceptance process
• Guarantors will only be contacted if payments are outstanding
• If you are a care‑experienced or sponsored student, please upload proof to the accommodation portal instead of a guarantor form
For more information about Guarantors, please see our FAQ's
How to apply
Applying for student accommodation is a five-step process:
To submit an application, please go to our accommodation portal . You will need to create an account with your student ID number (begins with H00). Once you have applied, we will email you to confirm that we have received your application. If you do not receive this, please email halls@hw.ac.uk to let us know. Offers of accommodation will be made from July onwards for students holding an Unconditional Firm offer.
Before you can proceed to accepting your contract, you must upload your guarantor form onto our portal. You can then accept your offer online by following the instructions in your offer email. Your contract is not valid until you have accepted your offer online. Please note, we can only make one offer of accommodation. Any further offers of accommodation will only be made subject to availability.
You will need to pay a 4-week advance rent payment within 48 hours of receiving and accepting your accommodation offer. You must accept your offer of accommodation online before making the advance rent payment. Please log into your accommodation account in order to do so.
You can also use bank to bank transfer via Convera . Please ensure that you provide within the reference your HWU ID number. If you wish to request a receipt, please email Student Service Centre . Please note that if you do not make payment of the advance rent payment through the accommodation portal this will not update.
If we don't receive your advance rent payment within 48 hours of sending you your offer, then your offer will be invalid and may be cancelled.
Find out how to pay for your accommodation.
Once you have accepted your contract, you need to complete your accommodation online induction, via the accommodation portal. As part of the induction process, you will be required to book an arrival slot. This is essential to ensure a smooth arrivals process.
Please ensure you bring your arrival pass and a valid form of ID, you do not need to print a hard copy, as long as you can access your arrival pass via your mobile phone. When you arrive on campus, please make your way to the Main Reception, where you will be issued your key and directed to your hall. For directions and travel information for Edinburgh Campus, please visit our travel pages .
For further arrival information please see our arrival Information page.

pages.title: Residence Life | Heriot-Watt University
pages.summary: Our Residence Life team is here to ensure the welfare and wellbeing of all resident students living on the Heriot-Watt campus.
headings: Visit WattLiving for all you need to know about living on campus
pages.extracted_text:
Residence Life
The Residence Life (ResLife) Manager leads a team of three ResLife assistants and ten experienced live-in wardens. They are a friendly first point of contact who are here to help ease the transition into campus life.
The team also host a busy calendar of events, creating an inclusive and welcoming community on campus. We encourage all residents to come along to our events as they are a great opportunity to meet your wardens and form new friendships with fellow resident students.
How ResLife can help you
The Residence Life Hub is a welcoming environment where all resident students can find support for any challenges they may be facing. The friendly team can offer practical information, emotional support and signpost you to relevant University services.
ResLife are here to help students who:
- are having difficulty settling in to halls or University life
- are facing conflicts with their flatmates, for example over cleanliness or noise
- require further support from the wellbeing or disability teams
- require support for mental health
- have any questions regarding campus life
Living On Campus
Visit WattLiving for all you need to know about living on campus
ResLife events
All our events are shared on Facebook, Instagram and X (formerly known as Twitter) ( @HWUReslife ).
Please visit WattLiving for help and advice on what you need to bring with you and details of all upcoming events.
ResLife FAQs
Contact SafeGuarding Services on 0131 451 3500 using the red phone in the corridor, or through the SafeZone App.
Please note, if you are locked out four times, you will be charged £50. This will happen after every four times you are locked out.
All Royal Mail parcels and mail requiring a signature will come to the parcel room next to the ResLife Hub. Please wait until you have an email from us confirming it has arrived then follow the instructions on the email to collect.
There is QR code in your kitchen to log and report non-emergency maintenance. General repairs are carried out by our Estates department after issues are logged on our system. Please see WattLiving for further information.
For any emergency maintenance please contact SafeGuarding on 0131 451 3500 (lack of power, securing rooms, leaks).
Our internet is provided by Glide. We have information leaflets available in the Hub with how to join the student network, or you can contact Glide by phone on 0333 123 0115, email at studentsupport@glide.co.uk or tweet @GlideStuHelp.
Please see our digital tour which will guide you through the steps you'll need to take to get connected on your device and ready to start your studies.
Each hall has a laundry room with instructions posted up on how to buy a laundry card and top it up, and how to use the app. If you need any help, please come to the ResLife Hub and we will assist. To report any technical issues please contact Circuit .

Undergraduate accommodation
Living on a university campus offers undergraduate students a vibrant community and convenient access to academic buildings and resources. It's an immersive experience that helps you make lifelong friends and set the foundation for your future success.
Eligible students from England, Wales, and Northern Ireland can access free accommodation for Semester One. For further details, please see more information here .

If you have some treats being delivered to halls, take a look at where and when you can collect post and parcels...
Parcel collection is from Gateway Building, when parcels arrive they will be placed in the mail cabinet located on the ground floor, outside the SafeGuarding control room.
Letter collection is from 9.30 - 10.30 am and 2.30 - 3.30 pm, Monday - Friday. If you are not able to check your mailbox during these times, you can arrange for a flat mate to collect on your behalf, as long as they have your written permission (we will ask for this before handing over any mail).

headings: ... Especially when you're getting settled in and making your room more homely
pages.extracted_text:
By
HWResLife
Posted 2 years ago
Wed 28 Feb, 2024 12:02 PM
... Especially when you're getting settled in and making your room more homely
Therefore please be aware of the following when it comes to your mail... ﻿
Any items sent through Royal Mail will be accepted and processed by the University’s central mailroom team. Letters and small items will be delivered directly to your mailboxes by the Mailroom team, while parcels and recorded items will be delivered to ResLife.
Once ResLife has processed the Royal Mail parcels, an email will be sent to your preferred email address notifying you of your parcel. To keep the Parcel Room running smoothly, please follow the instructions below:
- Use your own name on your parcel (that matches your student ID), and your full address including the hall and room number. If you use different names, the items will be returned to sender.
- Please ensure that you have an email from ResLife confirming you have a parcel before coming to collect.
- Collect as soon as possible and remember to bring your student ID (photographic ID.)
- You can only come for your parcel when the parcel room is open (6pm - 8pm, Mon-Sat)
- Remember, you cannot pick up parcels for anyone else but yourself! ﻿
Please be advised that any parcel that is not delivered by Royal Mail will not be handled by us, couriers will instead attempt delivery directly to your hall. The University takes no responsibility for these so please contact your courier directly if you need any help.
The parcel room is open Monday - Saturday 6pm - 8pm. Please note that anything that has not been collected after 2 weeks will be returned to sender .
The parcel room is located in the Christina Miller building.

pages.extracted_text:
By
HWResLife
Posted 2 years ago
Wed 28 Feb, 2024 12:02 PM
... Especially when you're getting settled in and making your room more homely
Therefore please be aware of the following when it comes to your mail... ﻿
Any items sent through Royal Mail will be accepted and processed by the University’s central mailroom team. Letters and small items will be delivered directly to your mailboxes by the Mailroom team, while parcels and recorded items will be delivered to ResLife.
Once ResLife has processed the Royal Mail parcels, an email will be sent to your preferred email address notifying you of your parcel. To keep the Parcel Room running smoothly, please follow the instructions below:
- Use your own name on your parcel (that matches your student ID), and your full address including the hall and room number. If you use different names, the items will be returned to sender.
- Please ensure that you have an email from ResLife confirming you have a parcel before coming to collect.
- Collect as soon as possible and remember to bring your student ID (photographic ID.)
- You can only come for your parcel when the parcel room is open (6pm - 8pm, Mon-Sat)
- Remember, you cannot pick up parcels for anyone else but yourself! ﻿
Please be advised that any parcel that is not delivered by Royal Mail will not be handled by us, couriers will instead attempt delivery directly to your hall. The University takes no responsibility for these so please contact your courier directly if you need any help.
The parcel room is open Monday - Saturday 6pm - 8pm. Please note that anything that has not been collected after 2 weeks will be returned to sender .
The parcel room is located in the Christina Miller building.
